topics.title: What Kinematic Sequence Actually Is
topics.subtitle: The 4-segment chain from pelvis to clubhead
topics.defaultPrompt: Explain what kinematic sequence is in a golf swing. Walk me through the four segments — pelvis, thorax, lead arm, and club — and why they need to fire in that order.
topics.promptTemplate: Explain what kinematic sequence is in a golf swing. Walk me through the four segments — pelvis, thorax, lead arm, and club — and why they need to fire in that order. {{skill_level_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: I'm new to this concept — use simple analogies like cracking a whip and avoid jargon.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: I understand hip-shoulder separation and basic swing mechanics — go a level deeper.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include peak angular velocities, proximal-to-distal energy transfer, and what TPI / TrackMan data shows about elite sequencing.

options.label: Quick Answer
options.promptFragment: Give me a concise mental model in a few sentences.

options.label: Detailed Explanation
options.promptFragment: Provide a thorough explanation with each segment's role described in order.

options.label: Feels & Cues
options.promptFragment: Translate it into what each phase should feel like in my body.

topics.title: Stall and Release
topics.subtitle: Why segments must slow down to fire the next one
topics.defaultPrompt: Explain the role of deceleration in kinematic sequence. Why does each segment — pelvis, thorax, lead arm — need to slow down for the next one to fire properly?
topics.promptTemplate: Explain the role of deceleration in kinematic sequence — why each segment must slow down for energy to transfer up the chain. {{skill_level_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: Use a simple analogy like a whip or a chain — I don't need physics terminology.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: I follow the chain concept — explain why deceleration is what actually transfers energy.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include conservation of angular momentum, kinetic link principle, and how deceleration of the proximal segment accelerates the distal segment.

options.label: Quick Answer
options.promptFragment: Give me the core idea in a few sentences with one good analogy.

options.label: Detailed Explanation
options.promptFragment: Walk through each segment's deceleration and how it fires the next link in the chain.

options.label: Feels & Cues
